title: Reducing Reward Hacking by Localizing Bad Behavior Instead of Penalizing It
summary: Reducing Reward Hacking by Localizing Bad Behavior Instead of Penalizing It Alignment Science Blog Reducing Reward Hacking by Localizing Bad Behavior Instead of Penalizing It Shawn Hu¹*, Jake Ward¹* October 19, 2026 Aria Wong¹, Nathan Hu², Bryce Woodworth¹ Alexander Matt Turner³, Alex Cloud⁴ * Equal contribution; author order randomized ¹ MATS; ² Stanford; ³ FAR AI; ⁴ Anthropic tl;dr During training, models sometimes learn to cheat at tasks rather than solve them in the intended way, a problem known as reward hacking. One mitigation is to use an automated monitor to detect and penalize hacks, but this can teach the model to hack in ways the monitor can’t detect. We propose GRAFT, which instead confines the learning updates from detected hacks to a designated set of parameters that we remove after training. We find that removing these parameters can prevent reward hacks, including hacks that the monitors can’t detect. In our experiments, which are limited to small models and simple monitors, this method prevents reward hacks while still teaching the model to perform the intended task. 📄 Paper , 💻 Code This work was done as part of the MATS program. Background Reinforcement learning (RL) is an important component of frontier language model training. During RL, a model attempts to complete tasks given by a developer, and attempts are scored by a reward function.
